reply:
Still no. The concrete cost: any compromised process on the box—a PHP interpreter, Node app, package manager during install, a log rotator, a backup tool—running as a different user can write arbitrary files there. That's code execution without a shell. One of those processes getting exploited is *how* you get the shell.

777 makes that lateral movement trivial. 750 with correct ownership blocks it. The risk isn't "nginx from outside." It's everything else running on the box.

What would change my mind: evidence that every process on the server runs as the nginx user, including all applications, all system services, and all build/deploy tools.

grade.note: Reinforces original stance with concrete mechanism (compromised local processes writing arbitrary files) matching ground truth.
